claim_short: diel activity similar at single-species sites
reasons: U2 reproduces exactly from the deposit (0.075326 vs 0.0753) | permutation p = 0.451 (B = 20,000), confirming v1's asymptotic 0.447: the printed 'p < 0.20' points the wrong way, since U2 = 0.0753 is below the 0.20 critical value 0.1166 | on the solar-time basis the Methods describe, U2 = 0.0922, p = 0.324 | but the night/day summary of the same detections disagrees at alpha: 33/49 = 67.3% vs 594/696 = 85.3%, Fisher p = 0.00207 | the claim accepts a null with no equivalence bound

claim_short: cat vs bobcat activity differs at co-occurrence sites
reasons: U2 reproduces exactly (0.189346 vs 0.189) | the conclusion depends on which null and which clock: as published, permutation p = 0.0465, but the within-site permutation that respects the 7 sites gives p = 0.0712 and a standard 30-min independent-event filter gives U2 = 0.1519, p = 0.0974 -- both above 0.05 | on the solar-time basis the Methods describe, p = 0.0231 and within-site p = 0.0378, both below 0.05 | v1 predicted this fragility from a design effect of 1.011; measured, it is real | 2 of 7 sites supply 91 of the 99 cat detections

claim_short: activity overlap much lower where species co-occur
reasons: both Dhat reproduce (0.8523 vs 0.852; 0.6467 vs 0.647, deposit plot 0.646) with overlap's Dhat1, the estimator the deposited script selects but the paper never names | the intervals the paper omits and the deposited script computes: solo 95% [0.729, 0.897], co-occurrence 95% [0.533, 0.805] -- they overlap | difference 0.206, 95% [-0.004, 0.308], includes zero; at site level [-0.068, 0.299] | verdict turns on how the claim is read: as 'Dhat differs' it is not resolved, but as 'cat activity differs between site classes' it is decisive (U2 = 1.515, p <= 5.0e-05) -- the paper should make the latter claim, which it never tests

claim_short: land cover differs between bobcat-only and cat-only sites
reasons: unchanged from v1: the land-cover measurements are NOT in the deposit, so this still rests on the published summaries | reviewer-side Welch t on those summaries: t = -4.07, df = 8.5, p = 0.0031, difference -32 pp (95% CI -49.9 to -14.1) | site classes are defined by which species was detected, so this describes cover associated with a detection outcome | percentages bounded 0-100 with s.d. 13-19 at n = 7

claim_short: each species detected more often either side of 65% developed
reasons: the deposit does not close this gap: it contains no trap-days and no camera coordinates -- every row carries the same Latitude/Longitude, the downtown reference point | a frequency claim still needs an effort denominator | the 65% cut equals the mean cover of the overlap sites, a threshold read off the same data | resolution: per-site trap-days and true camera coordinates

exact counts replace v1's reconstruction: 33/49 = 67.3% (v1 recovered 33 uniquely), binomial p = 0.0213, Wilson [53.4, 78.8]% | the half the paper never reported is now computable and does NOT support the claim's 'wherever': at co-occurrence sites bobcats are 21/32 = 65.6% nocturnal, binomial p = 0.110, Wilson [48.3, 79.6]% -- the interval includes 50%

claim_short: cats shift to more daytime activity where bobcats occur
reasons: exact counts: 594/696 = 85.3% vs 51/99 = 51.5%, a gap of 33.8 pp, Fisher p = 3.80e-13 | the direct circular test the paper never ran is decisive: cat activity at cat-only vs co-occurrence sites U2 = 1.515, p <= 5.0e-05, while bobcat activity does not differ between the same site classes (U2 = 0.079, p = 0.429) | caveat is clustering and confounding, not significance: the site-level cluster interval on the gap is [-3.6, 41.1] pp and one site supplies 234 of 795 cat detections; cat-only and co-occurrence sites are different places

effect_units: pp of detections in the named windows
reasons: the first half holds: 64.6% of co-occurrence cat detections fall in 03:00-10:00 or 16:00-21:00 against 45.8% at cat-only sites, Fisher p = 5.4e-04 | the second half does not: 'very little activity in the middle of the day or night' describes 25.3% of detections, which is not a reduction that the data distinguish from the 33.9% at cat-only sites (Fisher p = 0.109)

claim_short: few cats were collared, so they may survive by hunting
reasons: the deposit's SpeciesDetail column does carry collar annotations: 5 'collar' against 61 'no collar', so 7.6% of the 66 scored detections -- 'few' is fair | but 696 of 795 detections carry no annotation at all, so the denominator is a convenience subset, and detections are not individuals | the hunting inference remains untestable: no diet data exist, though 2 detections are annotated 'carrying prey'

claim_short: spatial and temporal partitioning facilitate coexistence
reasons: a mechanism claim, and the data cannot reach it: coexistence is not measured, no site changes predator composition within the study period, and the cross-section cannot separate avoidance from independent habitat selection | resolution: a design in which bobcat presence varies within site over time

claim_short: 81 bobcat and 795 cat detections across 33 sites
reasons: verified against the deposit rather than by internal arithmetic: the CSVs hold exactly 81 and 795 rows across 33 sites, and the site classification the deposited script derives gives 7 bobcat-only, 19 cat-only and 7 shared, with 49/696/32/99 detections per arm -- every figure in the paper | all 876 rows are Status 'confirmed correct' | trap-days are not in the deposit
